title: 2009 AMC 10B Problem 15
statement: When a bucket is two-thirds full of water, the bucket and water weigh \(a\) kilograms. When the bucket is one-half full of water the total weight is \(b\) kilograms. In terms of \(a\) and \(b,\) what is the total weight in kilograms when the bucket is full of water?

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the bucket’s weight and \(y\) the weight of a full load of water. Then \[x+\dfrac23 y=a\] and \[x+\dfrac12 y=b.\]

Subtracting gives \(\dfrac16 y=a-b,\) so \(y=6a-6b,\) and \(x=b-\dfrac12 y=4b-3a.\) The full bucket weighs \[ \begin{aligned} x+y &= (4b-3a)+(6a-6b) \\ &= 3a-2b. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(x\) be the empty bucket’s weight and \(y\) a full load of water
Subtract \(x+\dfrac12 y=b\) from \(x+\dfrac23 y=a\) to find \(y\)
